content: Sections are set apart by the subdivision, not by the tempo. Main groove: 11 notes per beat. Bridge: the 11-pattern is expanded and gets a hemiola. Breakdown: 7 notes per beat on the same pulse. The pulse and the click stay the same.
parameters: Section types named by Neely: groove, bridge, breakdown. 11 to 7 notes per beat = 0.64 of the note rate (computed)
where: Against the Fall of Night (title track)

item: Form in two halves with one melody
content: The melody is written to work in both feels. First half: the long pulses feel like the quarter notes of a 4/4 bar. Second half: the same cycle gets a quintuplet subdivision and feels like 7/4. The change comes half way through the melody.
parameters: Change point = middle of the melody. Audience dance: 2 steps right, 2 steps left; steps on counts 1 and 3 of 4 before the change, on counts 1 and 4 of 7 after it

item: Order of events in the longest track
content: From a drum transcription, in the order of the source: (1) set-up and 5/4 shuffle groove; the first minute repeats with small changes; (2) chorus; (3) after the second chorus the tempo drops; (4) drum feature in quintuplets, sextuplets, septuplets; (5) heavy half-time groove under a sax melody; (6) a second heavy half-time section; (7) horn fills and string stabs; (8) shuffle cymbal pattern in 5/4; (9) guitar solo by Plini; (10) 'five-on-the-floor' groove; (11) ambient outro.
parameters: Tempo drop at about 1:40 of 5:46 (29 percent of the length). About 11 events: one change each 31 s on average (computed). A reviewer: many sections in less than six minutes

content: Several tracks hold a groove and then break it near the end.
parameters: Hot Saturn: late turn to sixteenth-note syncopation. Thicc: heavy brostep transition. Perihelion: 'madcap' second half. Paydushko Horo: breakdown, then a calmer triplet feel

content: Intros: a bass line alone (Whalefall); a slow synth atmosphere in chillwave style (Macchina); an improvised drum intro (All These People); a piano figure played by a machine (Sequence Start); vocal loops (Perihelion); a direct start with the dense groove (Against the Fall of Night). Endings: an ambient outro (Whalefall); a flourish that resolves (Oeteldonk); a triplet feel that cools the energy (Paydushko Horo); a calm piano and strings track as album close; an '8-bit' album close (Cytherean).

content: Loud pieces alternate with quiet solo spots: a solo sax piece with live sampling, a bass solo with no accompaniment, a drum solo with changes of metre. content: A song is a chain of segments. Each segment loops one riff over 4/4. At the edge of the segment the riff is cut where it is, and a new riff starts on the next downbeat. There is no transition and no verse-chorus plan. Segments with voice and without voice alternate. Most songs have one guitar solo.
parameters: Segment lengths 8, 16, 24 or 32 bars of 4/4. The band learns the music in blocks of 4, 8 or 16 bars. Lengths of 12 or 15 bars do not occur

content: Nine riffs in one song. Riff A opens on one guitar with a lo-fi sound; then the full band plays it. After riffs B to D comes a solo section. A last section builds from riff H to riff I, the same idea one half step higher, as the climax with the voice. The first riff returns at the end.

item: Forms and dynamic plans of three Mockroot pieces

item: Typical plan of a bright fusion track (not confirmed)
content: Standard plan of the style, from listening experience and not from a source read in this study: riff intro; main theme (keyboard and guitar in unison); second theme; solos; heavy breakdown or clean interlude; last theme, often a step higher; short riff ending.

item: Short tracks that join into one sequence

item: Usual track form and the drop
content: Intro; main section with a bass drop; middle section; second main section with a second drop; outro. At the drop the percussion stops, often to silence, and then starts again with more force and a dominant sub-bass.
parameters: The bass usually drops after bar 16 or bar 32

content: A tutorial for the UK 140 style plans the track in blocks of 8 bars.
parameters: Intro 8 bars; build 8 bars; drop parts 1A, 1B and 1C of 8 bars each. At 140 BPM: 8 bars = 13.7 s; 16 bars = 27.4 s (computed)

item: Bar budget for a passage of 30 seconds
content: At 140 BPM one bar of 4/4 lasts 1.714 s.
parameters: 17 bars = 29.1 s; 16 bars = 27.4 s. Possible plans: 8-bar build + 8-bar drop; or 4-bar build + 12-bar drop; or a 16-bar drop with the build before the 30 seconds. At 150 BPM: 18 bars = 28.8 s. Computed values; the plans are an estimate

item: Build-up and the gap before the drop
content: The build-up repeats one figure, makes the drums faster and makes the volume grow. Many tracks have a break of half a bar or one bar before the drop. A vocal sample or a reverb tail fills the break.
parameters: The snare roll gets faster; synth swells rise; a high-pass filter on the full mix goes up; the energy below 100 Hz is kept for the drop

item: Snare roll and kick roll in the build
content: The roll doubles its rate in steps. Automation can make the pitch of the snare rise.
parameters: Roll of almost 8 bars: 4 bars with a snare on each beat, then eighth notes, then faster values. Kick build: double the number of kicks after 4 bars and double it again after 2 more bars

content: A short shouted voice sample comes immediately before the drop.
parameters: Sample of 4 words; drop at about 0:40 = about bar 23 to 24 at 140 BPM (computed)
